reviews.text:
She's currently 4 and a half years old. I've met the dog I love most in the world!

Until she was about 2 years old, she was very active, chewing on everything in the house and destroying it quickly, and she would always miss the potty pads when peeing and pooping. It was incredibly expensive and demanding to care for her.

But by talking to her every day, she learned simple words, her expressions are rich, and we feel like we can communicate somehow.

Lately, I've been able to intuitively understand how she's feeling just by looking at her face.

I've met the dog I love most in the world!

For first-time dog owners, there are many things you can't imagine, like how much it costs (like air conditioning).

They are born into this world with hope. When you bring them home, there are often many troubles from that moment, even that very night. I live alone, and even after coming home and going for a walk, I still have so much energy left that I want to play at night too, dashing around the room even after the lights are off ^_^; lol
I couldn't sleep because I had work the next day, so I would put a box over my head to prevent myself from being attacked every night lol

But even so, she's so much cuter than all that.

Dogs are very affectionate.

When you bring one home, please love her more than anyone else in the world ♪

Eight years ago, I adopted a male Miniature Dachshund from this shop, and this time, I was fortunate enough to adopt a female Long-haired Chihuahua from the same shop.

The Dachshund I adopted eight years ago is now eight years old, but he's still very healthy and happy every day.

He's a big eater, he brings his food bowl to me himself, and he loves people; he happily comes running when I call him. He's a very charming dog.

He's truly adored by my family and friends, and he's everyone's idol, with people even coming to visit him.

He's learned so many things, including "sit," "paw," "give," "stay," "spin," "high five," "jump," and "roll over."

And the Chihuahua I adopted this time is a one-year-old female.

She can be a little capricious and marches to the beat of her own drum, but when she wants affection, she'll ask to be held, and she'll bring toys to my hand as if to say, "Let's play!"

Her tiny body and earnest attempts to assert herself are incredibly cute, and she loves walks.

As this was our first time welcoming a Chihuahua, we had many questions and worries at first.

At that time, the shop staff told us, "Please feel free to call us anytime if you have any problems in the future," which was very reassuring.

We actually called them several times for advice, and each time they listened attentively and gave us careful advice.

It's truly invaluable for a pet owner to know that the shop doesn't just end with welcoming a dog, but that they continue to provide support and advice even afterward.

Also, when we welcomed our Dachshund eight years ago, the shop staff told us,
"Please talk to your dog a lot,"
and we still cherish those words.

Following those words, we've lived our lives talking to them a lot every day.

Now, they seem to understand many words; they'll go to the front door when we mention the names of family and friends, and they respond to what we say.

Every day, we tell both of them, "I love you," "Thank you," and "You're a good dog."

Both dogs are house-trained, enjoy walks, and rarely bark unnecessarily.

Their personalities are different, but even their playful rivalry for my attention is endearing, and they make me laugh every day.

They are both irreplaceable and cherished members of my family.

I felt the price was reasonable, but what impressed me even more was the kindness of the staff and their continued support and advice even after I brought my dog ​​home.

Eight years ago, I received excellent service from this shop, and it was such a wonderful experience that I didn't hesitate to welcome my new family member here again.

And once again, I feel so glad I chose this shop.

I highly recommend this shop to anyone considering welcoming a dog into their family.

If I ever have the opportunity to welcome another family member in the future, I would definitely choose this shop again.

Finally, I'd like to share some current photos of the two dogs I adopted from this shop 🐶♡

I am truly grateful for the opportunity to meet my Dachshund eight years ago, and for this Chihuahua.

I will continue to raise them with love and care, hoping they will both live long and healthy lives.

Thank you so much.

Shops like these must be banned. It's simply cruel. The animals are locked in small boxes, completely alone, each one on its own. The puppies are so tiny, without family, without siblings, without contact with other dogs. It's horrible!

This was the worst service. When I put my hand over the glass and said "It's cute," they must have thought I was a foreigner because they said "don't touch" and slapped my hand away without warning. I was so confused I just froze. The store smelled bad, the staff didn't know anything about service, and I wonder what the owner is doing?

The male employee in the back was not only jingling his keys to get my attention so he could take a picture, but he was also slamming them against the glass. It was awful.
I don't want him working in a job that involves handling people's lives.
He also made a disgusted face when I tried to go into the back of the store.
He didn't even say "welcome," which I thought was absolutely unacceptable! That's all.

You can adopt a cat 🐱 at this shop, or a dog 🐶 at their sister store in Sendai. They say the reasonable prices are because they don't spend on advertising. There are many cute kittens, so I recommend it. It's located in Kabukicho, so there's a lot of foot traffic and the kittens come and go very quickly. If you see a cute one, you should decide right away 😂 Thank you to the manager, Onodera-san, for your very polite service; you're a true customer service professional m(_ _)m
The sister store in Kichijoji smelled terrible, but this one was fine! I don't understand why the rating is low.

I don't usually write Google reviews, but I bought a puppy here about a month ago and am very happy with it.
To be honest, I don't really understand why there are so many bad reviews about this shop.
My puppy was well potty trained from the moment we bought him and hardly ever barked. I think he was well-trained at the pet shop.
He is still healthy and energetic, and has so much energy that it makes me a little tired.
I didn't notice any particular problems with the cleanliness of the shop, and the staff were very friendly.

The cat I adopted here
was soon found to have ear mites,
and then suddenly died a year later.

It may not have been the store's fault, but I feel so helpless.

PS:
I don't think ear mites were the cause of his death.
Two weeks after we adopted him, his earwax became severe, and we took him to the vet about four times for ear mites.
Please reconsider supporting businesses that keep animals in such conditions. Animals deserve proper care, not to be used for profit at the expense of their wellbeing.

Cute and reasonably priced. There are reviews saying the ear mites disappeared, but pet shops won't hand over the pets until they're cured. Did they properly clean the ears and take the pet to the vet?
Places like this should be closed by the authorities.
They're all so cute!
I saw this box-stacking system in Machida a long time ago, and I was surprised to see it being done in this form as I passed by; it seems like animal cruelty.
Animal abuse. The enclosures are extremely dirty, they live in their feces.

In the spring of 2017, we adopted a Ragdoll cat. We noticed symptoms resembling epilepsy, and took her to the vet for various tests, including genetic testing.

We discovered she had congenital disorders such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a single kidney, and brain abnormalities, and were told these conditions were incurable.

I didn't want to give her up, so I started regular checkups and medication.

However, last winter, she developed cardiomyopathy and kidney failure (due to the single kidney reaching its limit). Seeing her suffer during her hospitalization was heartbreaking. Fortunately, she was discharged, but we were told she had a short life expectancy.

Since then, I've become depressed, taken a leave of absence from work, and am caring for her while attending outpatient appointments. (Annual medical expenses are approximately 1 million yen.)

I live every day in fear, not knowing when we might have to say goodbye.

The contract states that we can exchange her for another healthy pet, but no pet owner would accept such a cruel thing. What do they plan to do with the sick pet if we return her?


As a pet seller, handing over an animal with a congenital disease means that I haven't fulfilled my obligations in accordance with the contract.
I've never regretted getting this animal, but please stop breeding and selling animals with genetic diseases!
I think anyone considering buying a pet should think twice.
If I don't receive an appropriate response, I will consider contacting the consumer center.
By the way, I bought a total of one dog and two cats from this store. The dog is still healthy, but one of the cats had ear mites when I bought it, and I was charged for the ear mite medication in addition to the price of the animal. (Normally, they would sell them after they've been cured!) I had already signed the contract when the ear mites were discovered, so I reluctantly bought the medication they recommended, but it didn't cure it at all, so I had to take the cat to the vet for about three months afterward.

----One Year Has Passed----
It took a year to finally get a response.
Fortunately, the animal is still alive and well.
For the sake of others, I hope for a faster response.
The animals and staff are completely blameless, so I have changed my rating to 5 stars.
----
The staff are all very nice people. It seems that vaccinations and preventative measures are properly taken, but since the animals are energetic during the day, it seems that illnesses that manifest at night may go unnoticed. It's understandable since they aren't watching them 24 hours a day.
They seem to manage and care for the animals properly, so they may not be held responsible, but as someone adopting an animal, if it was discovered to have an illness on the day of arrival, I think there should be some compensation for the costs. (Insurance wasn't 100%)
Animals are not "things" that can be easily returned, so the seller should also take full responsibility.
The response was too formulaic, so unfortunately I'm giving it 1 star.
If the subsequent response is good, I will change the rating, but if nothing happens, I will leave it as is.

---Additional Review---
Afterward, other illnesses (malformations) were found, and I inquired, but after being told "I'll ask my superiors!", the superiors' decision was simply "We'll exchange it." It's disappointing. The veterinarian's assessment is that it only has about a year left to live...
I don't know if it will make it to its first birthday,
but since I met it, I want to take care of it until the end. Maybe I just happened to get a puppy like that, but I think those who were able to get a normal, healthy puppy were lucky.
I want you to imagine what it would be like if my puppy was like that.
I doubt there will be any comments from the management on this review either!
The inquiry history should still be there... If there is any consideration for animals and sincere response to buyers, I will rewrite this comment.

How do we get these places regulated or shut down? These poor animals are literally roasting in their cages, it’s pathetic. I feel awful for them, little kittens cuddled up next to each other looked scared to death. Totally unpleasant to go into and I walked out because I did not want to give those people any indication that anyone was actually enjoying it in there. I felt horrible leaving the animals though and literally thought about them my entire trip. Bless them :”(
Its animal cruelty to have the pets in cages like that.

Told the staff multiple cages had no water and some were panting, others licking at their water trying to drink. Was acknowledged then walked back past a while later and he still hadn’t given them any water. Disgusting.

Please.
Please make the store cooler.
The dogs and cats are so cute, so I would like you to create an environment where they can live comfortably.
